description: This Python source file provides utility classes and methods for testing Dynamo's minifier functionality within the PyTorch framework. It includes classes for storing test results, setting up test environments, running subprocesses, and executing full minification tests, focusing on reducing Dynamo compilation failures to minimal reproductions.

classes.name: MinifierTestResult
classes.description: Dataclass for storing and processing minifier test results, including methods to extract modules and exported program paths from code strings.

classes.name: MinifierTestBase
classes.description: Base test class providing infrastructure for setting up test environments, running subprocesses, executing minification tests, and managing temporary directories for Dynamo minifier testing.

methods.name: setUpClass
methods.description: Sets up the test environment, including temporary directories and patching configurations.

methods.name: tearDownClass
methods.description: Cleans up the test environment, removing temporary directories unless specified to keep.

methods.name: _gen_codegen_fn_patch_code
methods.description: Generates code to patch code generation configurations for specific device and bug type.

methods.name: _maybe_subprocess_run
methods.description: Runs a subprocess, optionally in an isolated environment, handling code execution and configuration resets.

methods.name: _run_test_code
methods.description: Runs provided code in a subprocess and detects the directory of the minifier launcher script.

methods.name: _run_minifier_launcher
methods.description: Executes the minifier launcher script in a specified directory with given arguments.

methods.name: _run_repro
methods.description: Runs the repro script in a specified directory.

methods.name: _gen_test_code
methods.description: Generates test code with specific repro configurations.

methods.name: _run_full_test
methods.description: Performs a complete minifier test, including running the problematic code, minifier, and repro, and checking for expected errors.
